questions.q: What do plants need to grow?
questions.fact: Plants make their own food using sunlight.

questions.q: Which season comes after winter?
questions.fact: Many flowers bloom in spring.

questions.q: What falls from clouds when it is wet outside?
questions.fact: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water floating in the air.

questions.q: What color are most leaves in summer?
questions.fact: Leaves are green because of a special stuff inside them that catches sunlight.

questions.q: What part of a tree grows down into the ground?
questions.fact: Roots drink up water and hold the tree in place.

questions.q: What do we call a bear's cozy winter home?
questions.fact: Many bears spend the coldest months resting in a den.

questions.q: What can you see in the sky when sun and rain happen together?
questions.fact: A rainbow shows all the colors hiding inside sunlight.

questions.q: Which season is the coldest?
questions.fact: In winter, some animals grow thicker fur.

questions.q: What pops out of a seed when it starts to grow?
questions.fact: A tiny seed holds a whole plant inside.

questions.q: What do many leaves do in the fall?
questions.fact: Leaves turn red, orange and yellow before they fall.

questions.q: Which tree has cones?
questions.fact: Pine trees stay green all year.

questions.q: What do we call a little hill of dirt that ants build?
questions.fact: One ant colony can have thousands of ants.

questions.q: What is the wet stuff on grass in the early morning?
questions.fact: Dew forms when the air cools down at night.

questions.q: Where do fish live?
questions.fact: Fish live in rivers, lakes and the ocean.

questions.q: What do plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.fact: Plants also make the oxygen that we breathe.

questions.q: Which tree is the tallest in the world?
questions.fact: Coast redwoods in California can grow taller than a 30-story building.

questions.q: What is it called when an animal sleeps through the cold winter?
questions.fact: During hibernation an animal's heartbeat slows way down.

questions.q: What is it called when water rises into the air as vapor?
questions.fact: The Sun's heat makes water evaporate from oceans and lakes.

questions.q: What do bees carry from flower to flower that helps plants make seeds?
questions.fact: Bees spread pollen as they visit flowers.

questions.q: What kind of rock forms when lava cools and hardens?
questions.fact: Lava turns into solid rock as it cools.

questions.q: What do we call a tree that loses its leaves in the fall?
questions.fact: Maple, oak and birch trees are deciduous.

questions.q: What do we call the place where an animal lives and finds food?
questions.fact: A pond, a forest and a desert are all habitats.

questions.q: Which insect chirps by rubbing its wings together?
questions.fact: Crickets chirp faster when the weather is warmer.

questions.q: What is a river of ice that moves very slowly called?
questions.fact: Glaciers carved out many lakes and valleys in Canada and the northern U.S.

questions.q: What gas do plants take in from the air to make food?
questions.fact: People and animals breathe out carbon dioxide.

questions.q: What do baby frogs start out as?
questions.fact: Tadpoles grow legs and lose their tails as they become frogs.

questions.q: Which tree is the biggest in the world by volume?
questions.fact: Some giant sequoias are more than 2,000 years old.

questions.q: What do we call a group of trees growing close together over a wide area?
questions.fact: Forests cover about one third of Earth's land.

questions.q: What are the tiny openings in a leaf that let gases in and out?
questions.fact: A single leaf can have thousands of stomata.

questions.q: What do we call all the living things in a place plus their surroundings?
questions.fact: A pond is a small ecosystem.

questions.q: Why do leaves change color in the fall?
o: The green chlorophyll fades and other colors show
The Moon pulls the color out
questions.fact: The yellow and orange colors were in the leaf all summer, hidden by the green.

questions.q: What is the thin outer layer of Earth that we live on called?
questions.fact: Compared to the whole planet, Earth's crust is thinner than an apple's skin is to an apple.

questions.q: What is rock made from layers of sand and mud pressed together called?
questions.fact: Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock.

questions.q: What do we call the huge northern forest of pines and spruces that spreads across Canada?
questions.fact: Canada has one of the largest boreal forests in the world.

questions.q: What do we call a cold, treeless plain with frozen ground below?
questions.fact: The frozen ground under the tundra is called permafrost.

questions.q: What is it called when water vapor cools into tiny droplets and forms clouds?
questions.fact: You can see condensation on a cold glass on a warm day.

questions.q: Which layer of the atmosphere do we live in?
questions.fact: Almost all of our weather happens in the troposphere.

questions.q: What do we call animals that eat both plants and animals?
questions.fact: Bears and people are omnivores.

questions.q: In a food chain, what are plants that make their own food called?
questions.fact: Producers are the first link in most food chains.

questions.q: How old can some bristlecone pine trees get?
questions.fact: Some bristlecone pines in California were alive when the pyramids were built.

questions.q: What do we call trees that grow cones, like pine and spruce?
questions.fact: Most conifers keep their needles all year.

questions.q: What causes a rainbow?
o: Sunlight bending and splitting in raindrops
questions.fact: Each raindrop acts like a tiny prism.
